statement:
Research objective: Measure points per possession by how the possession started (after a defensive rebound, live-ball turnover, made basket or dead ball) and how much teams differ in exploiting live-ball starts.

Data: 2026-27 NBA regular season from 2026-10-20 to 2027-01-31 (development period), plus 2022-23 to 2024-25 seasons. The 2025-26 season is not provided. Fields: play-by-play actions (actionType, subType, clock, period, teamId, personId, scoreHome/scoreAway, shotDistance, xLegacy/yLegacy, shotResult, shotValue, description).
Unit of analysis to consider: possessions (about 142200 expected in the development period).
What would count as a meaningful finding: Reliable team-level differences in live-ball-start efficiency that are not explained by overall offense.
Validation: claims are tested on games from 2027-01-31 to 2027-04-12, which are sealed until every claim is registered. Planned approach: Split-half reliability within development; team ranking correlation between development and validation periods.

Register at most three claims. Each claim needs an estimand, a direction, a pre-specified test with a pass rule, and an analysis script that runs unchanged on the validation data.
permitted_memory: full history (all 384 records); no record uses 2026-27 data
